full_review:
The frozen reading.md is substantively accurate and appropriately limited to a body-reading and applicability review. I independently read every character of the supplied 91,800-character paper.txt, including the header, main sections 1–6 and every subsection, references, Appendices A–F and F.1.1–F.3, Tables 1–6, equations 1–20, captions for Figures 1–4, and the extractable Figure 4 mechanism and anonymized cases. I also read the entire pinned root author README, reading.md and source.json. All nine manifest references and the manifest itself match their frozen SHA-256 values. Versioned and default HTML are byte-identical, and the actual HTML watermark identifies 2609.37082v2, 30 Sep 2026. This is a manual static independent review of the supplied artifact, not a protected runtime ReviewSession authentication, original-result reproduction, full-PDF visual audit, or repository performance acceptance.

One required provenance reconciliation prevents an unconditional accept of the frozen bundle: source.json still presents two inherited interim statements without marking them historical. reading_observation says RL and results have not yet been read, contradicting full_body_complete, its complete actual_read_ranges, and reading.md. author_code says the author repository has not been pinned or read, contradicting its own author_repo object and reading.md's explicitly pinned README-only coverage. These contradictions do not reveal an error in the scientific reading; I have independently verified the body and README coverage now. They must nevertheless be explicitly superseded before the bundle is described as a coherent final current reading record. Preserve frozen originals and this original revise verdict. A separate, clearly authoritative correction/status artifact can identify both old fields by exact path and state their historical nature and current superseding observations. This correction is mechanical provenance reconciliation; it requires no additional paper review, scientific claim, experiment, model invocation, or old budget reset. It must not expand author coverage to code execution or authenticate a paper-to-code correspondence.

Mechanism check: sections 2.1–2.3 support Rubric–Answer–Verify, rejected-answer feedback into Answer, policy-generated next memory, q plus memory as the next context, token-budget refresh and preserved turn budget. The author's word independently describes role-based self-verification here; reading.md correctly does not substitute it for this repository's trusted independent acceptance or user criteria. F.2 requires only next_step_plan and task_progress at the top level. Knowledge_graph and navigation fields are optional, source_url is optional within facts, and nested additionalProperties restrictions are not universally specified. The immediately preceding checkpoint ID is exposed, with compact state by default and explicitly requested bounded conversation/structured tails. Character limits and the latest checkpoint are not a guarantee of complete correction, contradiction, provenance or dependency retention. The record accurately defers direct migration and avoids claiming a verified general knowledge graph or arbitrary historical retrieval.

Training check: equation 3 masks undesirable assistant turns from the loss and masks all non-assistant turns. Such turns can still condition later tokens; the record correctly avoids claiming that masking removes all historical contamination. Equations 4–5 and section 3.2 distinguish noisy terminal credit assignment from segment-induced trajectory reweighting. The 1/K alternative corrects total per-trajectory weighting but is empirically insufficient here. Final-segment training trains one last segment per trajectory, using GRPO-style group z-score and GSPO's exponentiated mean token log-ratio. Overflow becoming a failed final segment provides the described indirect incentive; it does not directly optimize all previous Seal arguments or prove universal stability. Section 4.1 gives the stated 35B-A3B, 256K, 512 turns, temperature 1.0, 96 GPUs split 32/64, all-state SFT and Answer-only RL. BrowseComp's extra Discard-All fallback is correctly isolated as an attribution limitation. Appendix C includes resource penalties, action-local violations/caps, parallel-tool bonuses and context-budget randomization. The record correctly avoids attributing the complete recipe to a single isolated change or treating rounds-plus-weighted-calls as observed wall time or spend.

Numbers and experiment check: Table 1 values and base comparisons in reading.md match the actual table, including metric differences and results that exceed Traverse. Table 2 GAIA 61.81 to 80.26, finance 38.36 to 58.06, shopping VPR .6660 to .6680 and SoP .2245 to .3576 match. F.3 explicitly excludes all 244 time-sensitive finance items and uses all 391 time-stable items from 635, not a random sample or the whole benchmark. The shopping rubric score is not verified purchase availability or downstream human satisfaction. Section 4.3 explicitly disables answer verification for the Figure 2 comparisons; BC185 SFT 60.4, all-segment 51.7, weighted 57.8, final-segment 65.2 and the stated WideSearch Row/Item-F1 numbers are all present in the body. Reported dynamic failures around steps 20 and 25–30 are body claims; I did not infer them from unexamined plotted points. The record correctly limits collapse evidence to the reported recipe and tasks and notes absent component-wise orthogonal ablations and uncertainty estimates.

Table 3 check: 54.95 to 65.23 Avg@3, 68.11 to 76.22 Pass@3 and 56.22 to 68.11 Maj@3 match. First-operation medians are conditional on having a memory operation: 217/231.4K versus 67/67.5K. Average trajectory turns include all trajectories and rise from 112.2 to 217.7. Thus earlier first sealing cannot support net token, latency or cost savings. The prose rounds the latter to 217, while the table is 217.7; reading.md appropriately preserves the table. Appendix D selects K retrospectively after a fixed permutation using five Bo1 and four Bo5 historical full-set evaluations. Observed 3pp/5pp deviations are calibration results and not future-model guarantees or an independent unselected holdout. Appendix A's uniqueness is explicitly approximate over the targeted KG/type/agent candidate union; tool-free filtering cannot prove zero leakage. Appendix B's two selected successes and Appendix E's three anonymized successes lack an outcome denominator and a controlled causal decomposition. The record makes these restrictions explicit.

Tools, judges and author boundary check: F.1 supports the default search count and returned fields, multi-URL question-conditioned summaries, and transparent backend retry/fallback. These do not certify equal backend cost or comprehensive evidence. F.3/Table 6 supports the specified judges, semantic equivalence, component FP handling, table normalization and alignment. The BC/BC-ZH embedded prompt explicitly ignores formatting inconsistency; it cannot certify this repository's output-contract or permission compliance. Not all benchmark evaluation prompts or implementations are embedded; the record correctly states that limit. The full author README supports separate harness versus model weights/training stack, deployment-specific unbundled backends, planned 8,617 QA release, MAX_VERIFY=3 example, independent Answer/Verify budgets, retry and resumption support, and a qualified Apache-2.0 licensing statement. I have read no author source modules, datasets, model weights, training implementation or experiment outputs and have executed none. The README bytes are verified; the supplied commit/tree/date pin is recorded but not independently reauthenticated against the remote Git object, and exact v2 experiment-code correspondence remains unknown.

Figures and visual scope: captions 1–4 and Figure 4's extractable text were read. The two local external SVGs' hashes match the supplied additional hashes and have no text tags. Only file/hash/extractability metadata were checked; I did not view pixels, trace vector glyphs, read plotted points, or perform any PDF/page audit. The phrase in reading.md about separately checking the independent SVGs should be expanded in the final report to avoid implying full plot verification. This is a nonblocking clarification because the relevant numbers and dynamic descriptions are present in the text I read.

Project fit and historical evidence: AGENTS, project_document_workflow and dual_main_workflow were read. GUIDE.md is empty and was only read; the guide README reiterates the human-only boundary. SYSTEM-99 remains open in TASK.md. I checked its current task detail's relevant initial Plan and ending progress excerpts, not its full 162KB history; I hash-checked the full file and the frozen legacy plan prefix, without treating that as full semantic review. The recovery report is read and preserves 59 matching, six missing, zero mismatching references in the five-package historical scope. I did not recover or re-review missing older originals or extend this review to their scientific claims. The proposal to use later real-host evaluations of counterevidence, rejected candidates, next actions, final quality and all-role usage is an evaluation direction only. Deferring Seal transplantation, checkpoint-only retrieval, self-verification acceptance, final-segment RL and automatic restart is consistent with the available evidence and repository contracts. No producer/public file, guide, stable Plan, tests, runtime, workflow, installation, model task, backend probe or publication was changed by this review. No empirical or performance claim for this repository is accepted. All older consumed Windows, FD, backend, Stage I and other budgets remain unchanged; this single new-paper review cannot close SYSTEM-99 or authorize a larger architecture migration.
